title: Phase 2 - Login page: credential derivation, secret lookup, session, route guard, four states

Claude-1.desc: PRODUCT invariant 7 states the OPPOSITE of what the brief's make32 does for non-BMP input: Array.from iterates code POINTS, so charCodeAt(0) keeps only each high surrogate and the returned array is SHORTER than 32, after which the loop reads undefined and undefined^x==x. TECH section 2's normalizeToCodeUnits returns 32 values always. The invariant-7 test would encode a false expectation as 'the brief's bytes' and go green on a derivation that does not match the original; the live proof cannot catch it because real credentials are ASCII.
Claude-1.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-2.desc: PRODUCT invariant 84 promises the `from` value carries path, search AND hash, but React Router strips the hash before a loader sees the URL - createClientSideRequest builds request.url via stripHashFromPath (router.js:2604-2605, 2762-2767), so new URL(request.url).hash is always ''. TECH section 5.3's mechanism cannot satisfy the invariant, and the guard test only asserts /login?from=%2F, a path with no fragment.
Claude-2.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-3.desc: TECH applies replace() unconditionally in requireSession, which destroys the referring history entry on an in-app link click and negates invariant 87. React Router defers history until redirects resolve and X-Remix-Replace forces REPLACE (router.js:981-999, 1024), so /login?from=... overwrites the entry the visitor came from. e2e/not-found.spec.ts:18-24 already performs exactly this PUSH. TECH's own e2e uses page.goto, a document load, where replace IS right - so the test passes while the in-app path is broken.
Claude-3.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-4.desc: PRODUCT invariants 14 and 97 contradict each other and their two checks are irreconcilable. 14 says the users path is never requested during authentication, 'not a single user record', and the network log holds 'nothing else'; 97 fetches GET /users/<id>.json on landing. M2's check asserts exactly one API request with no path containing 'users'; M4's asserts one request to /users/<id>.json. M4 must turn M2's check red, and no milestone says it is rewritten.
Claude-4.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-5.desc: Guarding / breaks six existing e2e specs (placeholder-routes, telemetry-buffer, accessibility, right-to-left, not-found, deployed-smoke), so M3's 'npm run e2e green' cannot hold. Worse, TECH's check for invariant 143 claims the placeholder is proven byte-unchanged BY those same tests passing untouched - and placeholder-routes.spec.ts is one of them. Invariant 137's 'not-found behaviour unchanged' is also false once its home link bounces a signed-out visitor.
Claude-5.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-6.desc: M2's claimed verification cannot go green with only M1 delivered: M2 performs a real sign-in that writes the session, but the KeyValueStorage instance comes from createRuntime, whose tabStorage field TECH schedules in M3, and writeSession is deliberately off the barrel so app cannot reach it either. Corollary: M2's sign-in writes a sessionStorage entry that telemetry-buffer.spec.ts:44-50 asserts is absent.
Claude-6.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-7.desc: Activating retry unmounts the alert containing the focused retry control, so focus falls to document.body - which invariant 110 forbids by name ('not on retry'). Invariant 44 has the same hole. TECH specifies no focus handoff; its own proposed check (activeElement !== body) would catch it, so the check is right and the design is missing.
Claude-7.disposition: resolved: focus handoff to the busy Login control added to invariant 60, carved out in 110. The confirmation rated it PARTIAL because invariant 44 still said 'moves focus nowhere' without the exception; 44 now carries it explicitly, verified as item 7 in evidence/reviews/g1-residue-verification.md

Claude-8.desc: PRODUCT invariants 44 and 55 assume the user submitted from the Login control ('focus stays on the Login control where the user left it'), contradicting invariant 107, which makes Enter inside either field a submission path. An implementer reading 44 literally moves focus to the control on submit, which 55's 'without moving focus' forbids.
Claude-8.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-9.desc: TECH section 3's /secrets narrowing does not exist in the shape it claims: FILE_ALLOWLIST maps a path to banned WORDS and is read only by checkExportedVocabulary, while the /secrets check is an unconditional literal-substring test in checkWholeScopeVocabulary (assert-domain-vocabulary.mjs:159-161) that never consults it. The narrowing needs a new mechanism, and M1's demonstrable-negative evidence depends on it.
Claude-9.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-10.desc: The redirect import ban lives in TWO eslint blocks, and TECH narrows only the first. The second (eslint.config.js:572-593, files: src/features/*/**) carries the identical ban and wins for feature files in flat config - which is exactly where src/features/auth/guard/** lives. Narrowing only 556-569 leaves the guards failing lint.
Claude-10.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-11.desc: Invariant 41's spinner and pressed-violet busy control have no mechanism: Button.tsx:41-52 renders only children (no spinner) and VARIANT_CLASS.primary paints primary, not primary-pressed, when not hovered; the kit exports no Spinner. This is a THIRD kit change invariant 141 requires be raised rather than slipped in, and TECH's map for 141 names only two.
Claude-11.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-12.desc: Invariants 76 and 125's 'or any substring of them' is literally unsatisfiable - one character of a password is a substring of it, and a 32-hex correlation id contains substrings of a 64-hex secret. TECH's checks quietly test whole-value containment instead, and the genuine intent (catching a truncated secret prefix in a log line) is covered by nothing. Neither invariant is in the review-dependent list.
Claude-12.disposition: resolved: duplicate of Codex-13, fixed once - invariants 76 and 125 restated as whole-value plus a twelve-character-window check, with the shorter-fragment residue disclosed as review-dependent. Confirmed in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-13.desc: Invariant 86's 'never painted, not even for a frame' is not decided by its proposed check - a domcontentloaded snapshot plus a later zero-count both sample discrete moments and a one-frame paint between them is invisible to both. The real guarantee is the structural argument in TECH 5.3, which is a review claim; 86 appears in neither review-dependent list, so that list is not complete as the section claims.
Claude-13.disposition: resolved: duplicate of Codex-19, fixed once - the no-flash check became a page.addInitScript MutationObserver installed before navigation, and invariant 86 moved to the partially-review-dependent list. Confirmed in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-14.desc: The header is a data surface with only skeleton/data/neutral, deviating from ARCHITECTURE.md's 'four states everywhere data is involved' without a decision-log entry. Invariant 29 argues the login page's exemption explicitly (it loads no data); the header DOES load data, so that reasoning does not carry, and this third deviation is neither recorded nor argued.
Claude-14.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-15.desc: TECH specifies Skeleton for the failed-name avatar, but Skeleton.tsx:39 hard-codes animate-pulse and line 38 sets aria-hidden - so the terminal failure state renders a permanently pulsing circle that says 'still loading' forever and is absent from the accessibility tree. Invariant 99 asks for a placeholder shape, not a loading indicator.
Claude-15.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-16.desc: Component tests of the success path have no router: renderRoute.tsx:73-81 renders ApplicationRoot with no RouterProvider or MemoryRouter, and TECH's only stated change adds a fake tabStorage and store. But the success path calls navigate(), and TECH specifies invariants 65, 66 and 130 as COMPONENT tests that reach it - useNavigate throws outside a router.
Claude-16.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-17.desc: M3 and M4 overlap despite the plan claiming strict sequence: M3 delivers the authenticated layout route 'and its lazy loader', but TECH 5.2 says authenticatedLoader ships with AuthenticatedLayout (M4) and section 6 says it calls store.read (M4's createSignedInUserStore), while section 5.1 says createRuntime gains tabStorage AND signedInUserStore in one change and M3's list names only tabStorage.
Claude-17.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-18.desc: No catalogue key exists for the correlation-id label the service-problem alert renders. Invariant 58 requires the id on screen and invariant 116 requires every user-visible string to come from a catalogue, but TECH's enumerated auth.json keys have no label for it - and vitest.setup.ts's empty-missingKeyReports assertion turns the omission into a test failure rather than a design conversation.
Claude-18.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Claude-19.desc: Invariant 22's proposed check ('an empty spy sink') is contradicted by the http client's own cancellation path: createHttpClient.ts:104-118 emits a debug log and a timing record with outcome 'cancelled' before returning, both of which reach the sink. The sink holds exactly those two, which is CORRECT under invariants 22 and 124 - the check, not the behaviour, is wrong.
Claude-19.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by a fresh re-briefed loop-spec-validator in evidence/reviews/g1-grill-claude-confirmation.md

Codex-1.desc: [converges with Claude-1] The specified non-BMP derivation differs from the brief's JavaScript. docs/task.md:40-44 vs PRODUCT.md:29-35, TECH.md:364-376. Codex recomputed for an astral character: 16 original units and secret C8...C869...69, versus the specs' 32 alternating units and C869...C869 - plausible secrets silently differ.

Codex-2.desc: TECH incorrectly claims the lookup inherits retry-on-timeout. createHttpClient.ts:103-133 returns 'timeout' immediately on a deadline abort, BEFORE shouldRetry is reached. Changing that modifies the http client despite invariant 141; leaving it contradicts the retry contract PRODUCT invariant 20 states.
Codex-2.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-3.desc: Returning the header promise directly from a loader BLOCKS navigation instead of enabling Suspense: router.js:2441-2446 awaits the loader's result, so a bare store.read() promise settles before rendering and the name skeleton and non-blocking page of invariants 99-100 never appear. The promise must be wrapped inside a synchronously returned object.
Codex-3.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-4.desc: [converges with the TECH risk] The proposed in-action ref does not suppress queued useActionState submissions: react-dom-client.development.js:8362-8367, 8434-8446 queues the second action and starts it only after the first succeeds - by which time the first action's finally has cleared the ref, so the queued action derives and requests again.
Codex-4.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-5.desc: The in-memory session shadow does not override stale VALID storage. readSession consults storage first and uses the shadow only when storage returns nothing, so a failed write over an older valid record authenticates the OLD user, and a failed removal can redirect a just-signed-out user back inside.
Codex-5.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-6.desc: Controlled credential state contradicts the credential-lifetime invariants: useState necessarily copies the password outside the field and keeps it after submission, while invariants 12 and 131 say it exists only as the field's value and is never copied into anything longer-lived. The proposed result-union test cannot observe that copy.
Codex-6.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-7.desc: Invariant 49 ('the URL stays /login when a submission succeeds') contradicts invariants 66-70, which navigate away on success. TECH silently implements the latter.
Codex-7.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-8.desc: The service-problem alert's placement conflicts with the required tab order: an alert rendered between the heading and the email field puts its retry button BEFORE both fields, while invariant 105 requires email, password, Login, then alert controls. No DOM structure is specified that satisfies both.
Codex-8.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-9.desc: [converges with Claude-7] Retrying removes the focused retry button with no focus handoff, returning focus to body, contrary to invariant 110.
Codex-9.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-10.desc: ARCHITECTURE.md still contains BOTH conflicts PRODUCT claims were amended: line 61 still requires a field-level error and lines 133-136 still say secrets never enter URLs, and its decision log ends without the promised phase-2 entries. Implementation currently has two incompatible binding contracts.
Codex-10.disposition: resolved: specs/ARCHITECTURE.md amended by the driving session - the runtime flow now reads 'null -> summary alert', the security posture separates the password from the derived secret, and nine phase-2 decision-log entries landed. Codex-11.desc: [converges with Claude-9] The proposed /secrets FILE_ALLOWLIST cannot affect the literal ban: FILE_ALLOWLIST is consulted only for exported vocabulary while the check at assert-domain-vocabulary.mjs:159-161 is unconditional.
Codex-11.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-12.desc: PATH TRAVERSAL: arbitrary string user ids are interpolated into a URL path without encoding. The accepted id '../secrets' resolves /users/../secrets.json to /secrets.json; '/', '?', '#' and backslashes similarly alter the resource - so a malformed secret response or a tampered session record can make the app fetch an unintended path.
Codex-12.disposition: resolved: user ids percent-encoded into the path AND restricted to A-Za-z0-9_- at the parse boundary, per the user's decision. Rated PARTIAL when PRODUCT's settled answer and TECH's file layout still described the permissive union; both now match invariant 18a, verified as item 1 in evidence/reviews/g1-residue-verification.md

Codex-13.desc: [converges with Claude-12] The literal 'no substring' privacy invariants are impossible and the tests weaken them silently: a one-character password overlaps ordinary JSON such as the schema version, while the tests check only complete credential strings and would pass if a prefix leaked.
Codex-13.disposition: resolved: the impossible 'any substring' claim in invariants 76 and 125 replaced by whole-value plus a twelve-character-window check. Confirmed by the raiser's own Codex thread

Codex-14.desc: Email trimming is an UNRECORDED change to the original derivation: the brief passes email directly to make32. Trimming inside deriveSecret changes the bytes for any stored address with boundary whitespace, and the live account proof is unlikely to discriminate it.
Codex-14.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-16.desc: The bfcache mitigation cannot establish invariant 103's no-render guarantee: pageshow revalidation happens AFTER a cached document is restored, so stale authenticated DOM may be visible before the redirect, and TECH admits the behaviour is untested.
Codex-16.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md

Codex-19.disposition: resolved: the no-flash assertion replaced by a MutationObserver installed through page.addInitScript before navigation. Confirmed by the raiser's own Codex thread

Codex-23.disposition: resolved: spec changed; confirmed CONFIRMED by the raiser's own Codex thread in evidence/reviews/g1-codex-confirmation.md
